name: NSSP Commercial Laboratory Data for COVID, FLU and RSV
category: Office of Public Health Data, Surveillance, and Technology
description:
The purpose of the National Syndromic Surveillance Program (NSSP) Commercial Laboratory Data source is to improve national situational awareness for conditions of interest to public health through enhanced laboratory data sharing between the CDC and external partners. Data are provided by five participating commercial laboratory companies operating in the United States: Labcorp, Quest Diagnostics, Aegis Sciences, ARUP Laboratories, and Perimeter (formerly Ginkgo Bioworks).

The NSSP Commercial Laboratory Test Volumes and Results by State - COVID-19, Flu, RSV dataset is a subset of the NSSP Commercial Laboratory Data source and includes test results for SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19), influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Not all participating laboratories contribute data for every condition. The volume and geographic distribution of reported testing may vary by laboratory, condition, jurisdiction, and time period. These data are aggregated across the commercial laboratories and reported at the state level. The period covered by this dataset begins on 10/4/2024, and the data will be updated once per week on Wednesdays. Data are submitted to CDC daily and processed typically within 24 hours using condition-specific inclusion criteria and result inclusion rules. Where sufficient information is available, multiple messages associated with the same specimen or accession are consolidated to present the most up-to-date version of the test results. Participating laboratories report results at the accession or specimen level rather than at the individual patient level; because multiple specimens may be drawn from a single patient for a given test, these records should not be interpreted as counts of unique persons tested.

This dataset includes laboratory testing for SARS CoV-2, influenza, and RSV. All conditions are represented using nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs), including polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and other molecular amplification methods. Percent positivity is calculated by dividing the number of positive NAATs by the total number of NAATs classified as either positive or negative for a given condition, then multiplying by 100 [(# of positive NAAT tests / total positive or negative NAAT tests) x 100]. Specimens for which the results are classified as unknown, indeterminate, or uninterpretable, or the test was not performed, are excluded from the calculation.
• Result inclusion: For each pathogen and associated laboratory test, specific LOINC codes and rules are used to select and synthesize laboratory results for inclusion in the dataset. Where sufficient information is available, multiple messages associated with the same specimen or accession may be consolidated to reduce duplicate reporting.
• Reporting of test results: Only test results that can be classified as positive or negative are included in applicable analyses. Unknown, indeterminate, or uninterpretable results are excluded.
• Data aggregation: Results are aggregated by week based on specimen collection date. As additional results are reported, values for prior reporting periods may change.
• Suppression: To reduce instability in estimates due to small numbers, counts and percent positivity are suppressed when the denominator (i.e., tests performed) or the number of positive tests is fewer than 10 tests. Zeros are not suppressed.
• Geography: State is assigned using the patient’s zip code of residence, or, where that is not available, the ordering provider’s zip code.

Details by Condition Condition:
COVID-19 - NAAT only: These commercial laboratory SARS CoV-2 data include both pathogen-specific molecular assays and results generated as part of respiratory pathogen panels. These data are intended to be used as a supplement to existing systems displayed on the NCIRD PRISM page. CDC recommends using complementary systems such as National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System, Respiratory Syncytial Virus Hospitalization Surveillance Network and the New Vaccine Surveillance Network to characterize the timing and severity of COVID-19 activity. Included LOINC codes: 94759-8, 94500-6

Influenza - NAAT only: These commercial laboratory influenza data are intended to supplement, rather than replace, CDC’s primary influenza surveillance systems. CDC recommends using clinical laboratory data available through FluView to assess the timing and intensity of influenza activity because those data provide greater testing volume and geographic representation. Included LOINC codes: 76078-5, 82166-0, 92142-9, 34487-9, 92977-8, 88193-8, 40982-1, 76080-1, 82170-2, 85478-6, 92141-1, 92976-0

RSV - NAAT only: These commercial laboratory RSV data include molecular RSV testing, including testing performed through respiratory pathogen panels. These data are intended to be used as a supplement to existing systems displayed on the NCIRD PRISM page. CDC recommends using complementary systems such as National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System, Respiratory Syncytial Virus Hospitalization Surveillance Network and the New Vaccine Surveillance Network to characterize the timing and severity of RSV activity. Included LOINC codes: 76089-2, 82176-9, 92131-2, 77022-2, 77023-0, 40988-8, 92957-0, 86040360

Data Interpretation and Limitations:

• Coverage and representativeness: These data are not a representative sample of all clinical settings or laboratory testing performed in the United States. Counts and percentages from participating laboratories should not be interpreted as direct measures of disease burden or total testing within a population. Participating laboratories vary in geographic reach, patient and provider populations served, testing portfolios, and types of data contributed to the dataset. Differences in observed testing patterns may reflect variation in healthcare systems, patient populations, provider and screening practices, laboratory market presence, client networks, and data-sharing arrangements. These factors can produce systematic differences between testing represented in this dataset and testing in the broader population and may bias comparisons or estimates when the data are generalized beyond the populations and testing settings represented.

• Geographic distribution: Participating laboratories collectively submit data from across the United States; however, geographic representation is not uniform. HHS Region 2 (New York, New Jersey, Puerto Rico) is the most heavily represented and HHS Region 6 (Arkansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas), HHS Region 7 (Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska) and HHS Region 8 (Colorado, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Utah, Wyoming) are the least represented. Geographic distribution also varies by condition because healthcare providers differ in their test ordering practices from each of the participating laboratories. The presence or volume of commercial laboratory data within a jurisdiction should not be interpreted as a complete measure of testing availability, testing activity, or the proportion of all laboratory testing captured within that jurisdiction. Population measures may provide contextual information about the geographic distribution of submitting testing; however, the dataset is not a population-based or a random sample. Population size therefore should not be interpreted as a denominator for laboratory coverage or representativeness, nor does it directly measure the proportion of a jurisdiction's laboratory testing represented in the dataset. It also does not account for differences in laboratory market share, provider networks, healthcare utilization, test-ordering practices, or the proportion of total testing captured within a jurisdiction.

• Condition-specific interpretation: Testing methods, laboratory participation, and reporting practices may differ across conditions. Testing volumes and other measures should therefore be interpreted within the context of each condition and should not be assumed to be directly comparable across conditions.

metadata.rowLabel: Each row represents the number of laboratory tests performed with results considered either positive or negative, and the number of those tests with results considered positive for the specified pathogen for the specified state. Each row also includes the percent of performed tests that were considered positive.
